items.title: Mother, son killed in Temerloh tanker crash laid to rest
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The remains of a mother and her 12-year-old son who died in a crash involving a tanker lorry and a car along Jalan Temerloh–Triang near Kampung Lebak last Friday were laid to rest at the Kampung Sanggang Muslim Cemetery here today. Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, was buried beside her son, Muhammad Fattah Aisy Naufal Saifulnizam, 12, in a joint funeral after Friday prayers, with the burial completed at 2.30pm. Saifulnizam said he last saw his wife and son on Tuesday before returning to Kampung Gadung, Sendayang, Negeri Sembilan, to manage his freshwater fish farming ponds.

items.title: GLCs, GLICs are public trust, not political property, says CSO Platform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) must be treated as institutions of public trust, not "political property", says the CSO Platform for Reform. The coalition said lessons from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji should extend beyond the pilgrims' fund to all state-linked entities entrusted with public assets and resources. "GLCs and GLICs manage assets and resources of significant public interest.

items.title: Alam Maritim fell to six-month low following MACC remand of CEO Azmi Ahmad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Alam Maritim Resources Bhd fell to near six-month low today after its group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad was remanded by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist an ongoing investigation. At 3.40pm, the counter fell three sen, or 11.54 per cent, to 23 sen, with 1.44 million shares changing hands, marking its highest trading volume in more than two months. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Zahid chairs road safety panel, maps congestion fixes before Johor Bahru RTS January debut
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 17 — Plans are being drawn up to ease traffic congestion in Johor Bahru city centre and prevent new bottlenecks from emerging ahead of the launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plans involved coordination among agencies and integration of public transport systems, as travel patterns were expected to change, particularly around the city centre and areas directly connected to the system. The system will connect Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru with Woodlands North in Singapore.

items.title: Singapore halts construction waste exports to Johor with immediate effect
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Singapore has halted all exports of construction and demolition (C&D) waste to Malaysia with immediate effect following concerns over alleged illegal dumping in Pontian. Johor Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said the decision was conveyed by Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) during a phone call today. During the call, Johor SWCorp emphasised that any waste export to Malaysia must strictly comply with existing laws and obtain prior approval from relevant local enforcement agencies.

items.title: In Bangkok's gun district, traders say Thai crackdown misses the mark
items.summary: Like all the gun shops in Thailand, it has been banned from importing firearms since a 2023 shooting at a Bangkok mall — one of several mass shootings, including at a school and a childcare centre, that have periodically prompted tighter regulation in a country with the second-highest private gun ownership in Asia. "I do still have hope, because like I've said, selling guns is less tiring than selling bread," said Warintorn, who also owns a baking school. In the capital's historic gun district, Thititorn Bupparamanee, president of the Firearms Traders Association of Thailand, said the suspension of permits would not fix the country's gun violence problem.

items.title: Carpenter in restaurant attack case sent for psychiatric assessment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A carpenter charged with causing grievous hurt to a businessman in a restaurant attack has been ordered to undergo a month-long psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta. Sessions Court Judge Noridah Adam made the order last week following an application by defence lawyer Mohd Ruzaini Zulkifli on behalf of his client, Wong Weng Luen, 49. The court fixed Sept 17 for an update on the psychiatric assessment.

items.title: No drug cartel in Genting: Pahang police stress immediate action if reports are lodged
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 17 — Pahang police have denied viral claims on social media that a large-scale drug cartel is operating in Genting Highlands, Bentong, without any enforcement action being taken. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said police would conduct an investigation and take appropriate action if such illegal activity was detected. The social media user claimed that no action had been taken despite several police reports being lodged.

items.title: Iran blames US presence for Gulf waters pollution after oil spills
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday blamed pollution in Gulf waters on US military operations in the region, after several oil spills were reported. "This environmental damage stems from the US military presence and the wars it has waged in the region over the past five decades," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told a news briefing. Last week, Iran called for compensation after an oil slick in the Strait of Hormuz reached the island of Qeshm, affecting beaches and an environmentally sensitive mangrove forest.

items.title: EPF contributions hit RM33.87bil in Q2 on higher membership, voluntary savings
items.summary: The latest quarterly contribution continues the upward trend, from RM20.61 billion in Q2 2021; RM21.68 billion in Q2 2022; RM24.65 billion in Q2 2023; RM27.42 billion in Q2 2024 and RM31.21 billion in Q2 2025. The continued growth in contributions and membership underscores the strengthening of EPF's contribution base, supported by steady employment growth, greater participation in voluntary savings and increased use of its digital platforms. For the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), voluntary contributions reached RM14.15 billion, reflecting sustained participation in additional retirement savings.

items.title: Alam Damai house goes up in flames, Bomba suspect EV charging in foyer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A two-storey terrace house in Alam Damai, Cheras, here, was destroyed in a fire early yesterday morning believed to have been caused by an electric vehicle (EV) that was being charged in the foyer of the house. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations division assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar in a statement today said his department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 5.03 am before a team of personnel from the Cheras, Sungai Besi and Bandar Tun Razak Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were rushed to the location. Ahmad Mukhlis said upon arriving at the location of the incident, his department found that the two-storey terrace house was 100 per cent burnt down.

items.title: Auku repeal offers chance to reset higher education, says UPM VC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) offers a timely chance to reset the country's higher education landscape, says Universiti Putra Malaysia vice-chancellor Datuk Professor Ahmad Farhan Mohd Sadullah. He said the move should pave the way for greater autonomy for universities, with the Higher Education Ministry focusing on policy while institutions are given more room to manage their operations. "I welcome this move as it provides an opportunity to reset higher education.

items.title: EPF's 1H26 investments income hits RM57.5bil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) recorded a 48 per cent surge in investment income to RM57.5 billion for the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), driven by strong global equity markets and gains from its international portfolio. Investment income for the second quarter alone rose 44 per cent to RM29.77 billion from RM20.61 billion in the corresponding period last year, with equities contributing RM20.94 billion, or 70 per cent of the quarterly total. Fixed-income instruments contributed RM6.91 billion, accounting for 23 per cent of total investment income.

items.title: Ex‑JKR officer tells High Court Muhyiddin made no calls to help Nepturis in RM141m Jana Wibawa project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A former senior Public Works Department (JKR) officer today said he did not receive any phone calls from then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin to help the contractor of a RM141 million government project, the High Court heard today. Former Selangor JKR director Lokman Nasir, 62, said this while testifying as the 23rd prosecution witness in Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia president Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial. Lokman was in charge of supervising progress on the RM141 million project to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD), which was won by contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Pickleball stars confirmed for Malaysia's first PPA Tour Asia event
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's top pickleball players will take on some of the world's leading professionals at the Leapmotor Kuala Lumpur Cup 2026, scheduled from Sept 9 to 13 at The Hood, Kuala Lumpur. Organised as part of the Professional Pickleball Association Asia (PPA Asia) Tour, the tournament will bring international stars to Malaysia alongside the country's leading homegrown talent, giving fans the opportunity to watch world-class pickleball on home soil. MALAYSIA'S TOP PLAYERS LEAD LOCAL CHALLENGE Among the confirmed Malaysian players are: Jimmy Liong (Kai Long) Malaysia's highest-ranked international pickleball player, Jimmy Liong brings extensive experience competing on the world tour.

items.title: Health Ministry creates 607 posts, approves RM1.57bil for Sabah healthcare
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry has created 607 new positions in Sabah as of Aug 1 this year to ensure state healthcare facilities operate at optimal capacity. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the new posts comprise 355 managerial and professional positions, including 77 specialist roles and 203 medical, dental, and pharmacy officers, as well as 252 implementation group positions. The new projects include the RM125 million Sabah Heart Centre and the RM81.95 million Type 5 Health Clinic with quarters in Sapulut, Nabawan.

items.title: Search teams comb rubble in Colombia nearly a week after quake as aid effort expands
items.summary: BOGOTA: Search teams worked through the rubble of collapsed buildings in western Colombia on Sunday, nearly a week after a powerful earthquake devastated cities and towns across the country's west, killing hundreds and leaving many more missing, injured or homeless. The 7.4-magnitude quake struck Monday morning in San Jose del Palmar, causing severe damage from the Pacific port of Buenaventura to Colombia's coffee-growing region and major western cities including Cali and Pereira. Official estimates issued late on Saturday put the death toll at around 290, with 140 people still missing and nearly 4,000 injured.

items.title: JDT's Sultan Ibrahim Stadium recreated with 400k Lego bricks
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A Lego brick replica of the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, home of Johor Darul Ta'zim FC (JDT), was unveiled at Legoland Malaysia Resort yesterday. Legoland Malaysia Resort vice-president CS Lim said the attraction showcased a modern Johor landmark and the state's football culture. JDT chief operating officer Alistair Edwards said the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium represented Johor's ambition, unity and passion for football.

items.title: Muhyiddin graft trial: Nepturis got RM16.4mil for police HQ, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Construction company Nepturis Sdn Bhd received RM16.4 million from the government for the Klang North District Police Headquarters project in Selangor under the Jana Wibawa programme, the High Court heard today. Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) director Lokman Nasir, 62, confirmed the payments after being shown government payment vouchers and payment instructions from the state PWD to Nepturis totalling RM141 million. Nepturis is among companies linked to charges faced by former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin involving alleged abuse of power and money laundering over the Jana Wibawa programme.

items.title: Sabah sets aside nearly RM1b to unlock state agriculture, industry and tourism potential
items.summary: KENINGAU, Aug 17 — The Sabah State Government has allocated nearly RM1 billion for the development of the agricultural, industrial and tourism sectors which continue to be among the main drivers of Sabah’s economic growth this year. In this regard, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor wants district officers to look into the economic potential in their respective areas. Some have tourism potential.

items.title: Caprice ordered to apologise, pay RM220,000 to Ebit Lew for defamation
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Rapper Caprice has been ordered to apologise and pay RM220,000 in damages to preacher Ebit Lew for defamation. The court further restrained Caprice from making any future comments or statements concerning Ebit Lew, whose real name is Ebit Irawan Ibrahim Lew, 42. Ebit Lew had filed the suit over a video uploaded by Caprice on Sept 15, 2023, featuring Mondy, which he claimed contained defamatory allegations.

items.title: Azman: Anwar not seeking to strengthen Umno at DAP's expense
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is not seeking to strengthen Umno at the expense of DAP, said his political secretary and Federal Territories PKR chief Datuk Azman Abidin. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported Azman as saying that Anwar's close working relationship with Umno leaders should not be interpreted as an effort to strengthen the party or weaken DAP. Azman said Anwar's role was to manage the multi-party unity government responsibly and work with all parties in the administration.

items.title: Thailand's second-quarter GDP grows 1.9pc year-on-year
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's economy grew 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from a year earlier, official data showed yesterday, higher than the median forecast of 1.7 per cent in a Reuters poll of analysts. In the January-March quarter, growth was 2.8 per cent on the year and a revised 0.6 per cent on the quarter. For the whole of 2026, the agency predicted the economy to grow 2.0 to 2.5 per cent, compared with a previous forecast of 1.5 to 2.5 per cent growth.

items.title: Bollywood stars told to drop surrogate ad in Indian state's food safety drive
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Three top Bollywood actors, including Shah Rukh Khan, must stop appearing in surrogate advertisements of a brand mostly associated with a banned beetle nut product, India's Maharashtra state has said in a warning as it intensifies a food safety drive. In a warning to Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff, made public over the weekend, the state said the actors were promoting Vimal's cardamoms but the brand is associated largely with a prohibited beetle nut mix - called pan masala - sold in tiny 3.5 rupees (US$0.0366) packs and considered harmful, especially when mixed with tobacco. Industry estimates show India's pan masala market was worth an estimated US$5 billion last year.

items.title: Police deny drug cartel operating in Genting Highlands
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang police have denied viral claims on social media that a large-scale drug cartel is operating unchecked in Genting Highlands, Bentong. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said police will investigate and act if any illegal activity is detected. "If a police report involving illegal activity is lodged, we will immediately investigate and take appropriate action, regardless of the location," he said at the Pahang police headquarters today.

items.title: Royal death brings early closure to Kelantan Heritage Weapons Festival in Kota Bharu
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 17 — The Kelantan Heritage Weapons Festival 2026 has been closed today following the death of a member of the Kelantan royal family. The closure follows the death of the aunt of the Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V, Datuk Tengku Salwani Almarhum Sultan Yahya Petra, at 6.10 am this morning at the age of 82. Confirmation of the death was made through the Sultan of Kelantan’s Office in a statement here today.

items.title: Sabah Heart Centre given top priority, Dzulkefly concedes staffing shortage remains a challenge
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Construction of the RM125 million Sabah Heart Centre is expected to begin in the third quarter of next year, with the facility targeted for completion and operation by the third quarter of 2029, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today. The project is among seven new health projects approved for Sabah under RMK-13 Rolling Plan 1, which has allocated RM1.57 billion for 53 health projects in the state, including 46 ongoing projects and seven new projects. Dzulkefly said the Heart Centre would be given top priority by the Health Ministry, with the RM125 million allocation covering the overall project, including upgrading works, equipment procurement and related preliminary works.

items.title: AmFIRST REIT's Q1 FY27 PAT more than double on higher occupancy, lower property expenses, finance costs
items.summary: Profit after tax rose RM3.4 million during the quarter from RM3.3 million a year earlier, while realised net income from operations increased 10 per cent to RM5.6 million from RM5.1 million. Revenue from operations grew 7.5 per cent year on year (Y-o-Y) to RM27.2 million, supported by stronger rental and car park income, as well as higher contributions from its co-working space operations. Overall portfolio occupancy improved to 88.3 per cent from 83.1 per cent a year earlier, reflecting stronger tenant take-up across several properties.

items.title: Kushner to hold talks with Netanyahu after rare meeting with Hamas
items.summary: TEL AVIV: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is due to meet Donald Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner on Monday, a day after he held a rare meeting with Hamas officials in Cairo, in a bid to push forward the US president's Gaza peace plan. A diplomatic source said Hamas leader Khalil Al-Hayya was present at some of the meetings that mediators held with Kushner and Trump's Board of Peace envoy for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, in Cairo on Sunday. Trump said in late July a deal was reached for the complete disarmament ‌of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

items.title: JB traffic dispersal plan being drawn up ahead of RTS Link operations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Plans are being drawn up to ease traffic congestion in Johor Baru city centre and prevent new bottlenecks from emerging ahead of the launch of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plans involved coordination among agencies and integration of public transport systems, as travel patterns were expected to change, particularly around the city centre and areas directly connected to the system. Loke also said the Transport Ministry (MoT), in collaboration with the Johor state government, was drawing up a traffic dispersal plan to strengthen the existing public transport system, including expanding the BAS.MY service network to 28 routes involving 254 buses, including electric buses.

items.title: JHM eyes FY26 turnaround on automotive, semiconductor growth
items.summary: The group is targeting 20 per cent to 30 per cent revenue growth in FY26, with a net margin of four to six per cent, followed by another 10 per cent growth in FY27, excluding new project wins. RHB Research said full lamp assembly programmes for new Proton models based on the advanced modular architecture platform are expected to contribute RM50 million to RM55 million annually, while a second model slated for production in 2027 could add another RM15 million to RM20 million a year. Automotive capacity utilisation remains healthy at about 80 per cent to 90 per cent.

items.title: Road crashes cost Malaysia up to RM30b a year, but human cost of 18 daily deaths is far greater, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysia incurs up to RM30 billion in socio-economic losses each year due to road accidents, said Works Minister Dato Sri Alexander Nanta Linggi. Nanta said the findings on the socio-economic impact of road accidents were presented at the Cabinet Committee on Road Safety and Congestion meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said that last year alone, road accidents claimed 6,537 lives, equivalent to an average of 18 deaths a day.

items.title: Aliff Syukri allowed to hold off apology to ex-minister Kadir pending appeal
items.summary: Aliff's lawyer Mahmud Abdul Jumaat said the court also allowed his client's proposal for the RM250,000 damages awarded to be paid into Abdul Kadir's solicitors' stakeholder account pending the disposal of the appeal. On April 29, Roslan, in allowing Abdul Kadir's suit, ordered Aliff to pay RM250,000 in damages over defamatory statements alleging unpaid investment debts amounting to millions of ringgit. The court also ordered Aliff to pay RM50,000 in legal costs.

items.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing heads to Russia for official visit, state media reports
items.summary: NAYPYIDAW: Myanmar junta chief-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing left for Russia on Monday for his first official visit to the country since he assumed the presidency in April, according to state media. Russia will be the fifth country Min Aung Hlaing has visited since becoming president, with official trips to India, China, Laos, and earlier this month, Thailand. Min Aung Hlaing's latest trip includes a Myanmar-Russia business forum.

items.title: Shein eyes company valuation of around US$25bil in Hong Kong IPO
items.summary: HONG KONG: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein is eyeing a company valuation of around US$25 billion in its Hong Kong IPO, said three people with knowledge of the matter, down from nearly US$100 billion four years ago due to challenging business conditions. Singapore-headquartered Shein, known for selling US$5 dresses and US$10 jeans to shoppers in about 160 countries, is aiming to launch its much-awaited initial public offering later this week, Reuters has reported. One of the three sources said that the company, which was founded in China in 2012, was looking at a valuation of between US$25 billion and US$28 billion based on the marketing price band for the offering.

items.title: Gold gains on weaker dollar, reduced Fed rate-hike bets
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold drifted higher on Monday, supported by a weaker dollar and recent soft economic data that reduced expectations for a US interest rate hike next month. Spot gold rose 0.60 per cent to US$4,400.15 per ounce by 0710 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.40 per cent higher to US$4,456.50.

items.title: Johor shuts Kulai factory after Jalur Gemilang, state flag found upside down
items.summary: KULAI: An industrial factory here has been temporarily closed after the Jalur Gemilang and Johor flag were found displayed upside down. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the incident was being viewed seriously as both flags represented the identity, dignity and sovereignty of the country and state. Jafni said the Kulai district officer was also coordinating follow-up action with MPKu and relevant agencies to ensure appropriate action was taken under existing laws.

items.title: Ministry defends transfer of Sabah hospital director amid ongoing sexual harassment probe
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — The Health Ministry’s decision to remove a Sabah hospital director from his post and transfer him to the state health department is pending further investigation into allegations of sexual harassment. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the administrative transfer was made deliberately to ensure the investigation could proceed without the officer remaining in a position that could potentially affect the process. His comments came after the hospital director’s lawyer, Joan Goh, said he was mulling taking legal action over the transfer.

items.title: Fires near Greek capital controlled after claiming two lives
items.summary: ATHENS: Two fires on the Greek island of Salamis near Athens that claimed two lives and led to the evacuation of nearly 600 people have been largely extinguished, the fire service said Monday. "The situation is better, there is no active front," a fire department spokesman told AFP, adding that two helicopters and over 200 firefighters remained in the area. Though the civil protection agency quickly issued evacuation orders, the fire department said the fires spread in just seven minutes owing to strong winds, trapping an elderly couple near their home.

items.title: O&G sevice provider Alam Maritim Resources says CEO Azmi Ahmad under MACC remand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd today announced that its group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad is under remand to facilitate an ongoing investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). The service provider to the oil and gas industry said the remand is for the purpose of facilitating the ongoing investigation and does not constitute any finding of wrongdoing. “The board has taken the necessary measures to ensure continuity of the group’s operations and will make further announcements should there be any material development,” it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.

items.title: Baby Eden’s arrival makes Mahathir great‑grandfather, Ally Mukhriz celebrates newborn online
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — A new chapter has begun in the storied Mahathir family, as Ally Mukhriz — daughter of Parti Pejuang Tanah Air president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir — has given birth to her first child, a baby boy named Eden Zakaria Ezran Cheah. Born on Sunday morning at 8.48am, weighing 2.9kg, Eden is not only Ally and her husband Ezran Daud Cheah’s first child, but also the very first great grandchild of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. Ally, whose full name is Meera Alyanna Mukhriz, shared the joyful news on Threads: “Ezran and I are happy to announce the birth of our baby boy, Eden Zakaria Ezran Cheah.

items.title: DOE: Air quality mostly moderate nationwide, Johan Setia stands out with unhealthy reading 137
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 17 — Johan Setia in Selangor recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 137 at 1pm today, the only location nationwide to report unhealthy air quality, the Department of Environment (DOE) said in a statement. The DOE said it had intensified patrols and drone monitoring in Johan Setia but found no open burning. The DOE said overall inspections found conditions in Johan Setia were under control, with no open burning detected at the time.

items.title: Room to grow: 524 classroom projects worth RM668m in the works for 2027
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 17 — A total of 524 additional classroom projects worth RM668 million are underway nationwide for the Year One intake in the 2027 session, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan. Kedah followed with 93 (92 approved), while Johor recorded 47 (45 approved). “Terengganu has 45 projects and Penang 30, all with LoAs.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines pilots cleared in drug tests, MAG moves to cabin crew screening phase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed a mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, with every test returning negative, the company said in a statement today. MAG said the exercise, concluded on August 15, covered all operationally active pilots. The group will now begin screening approximately 2,840 Malaysia Airlines cabin crew, starting August 18 and targeted for completion by September 3.

items.title: UUCA repeal can give Malaysian universities room to compete globally, says local varsitities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — The country’s new higher education legal framework must provide a conducive environment for Malaysian universities to grow, remain competitive and achieve excellence on par with leading institutions worldwide. International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Osman Bakar said the framework should be progressive, fair and forward-looking, while safeguarding the sustainability and integrity of universities. He said the move to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) presented an important opportunity to establish such a framework and empower universities to respond to the changing demands of an increasingly dynamic higher education landscape.

items.title: Pahang police investigate vandalised Bukit Tinggi temple statue, but no CCTV, no witnesses
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 17 — Police have received three reports regarding the incident of a statue at a non-Muslim place of worship being vandalised in Bukit Tinggi, Bentong, yesterday. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the three police reports were made by a 49-year-old security guard, a 45-year-old monk and a 41-year-old man. Meanwhile, Azry Akmar said his party viewed the incident seriously and investigations were still underway to identify the cause and the parties involved.

items.title: Don’t just scrap UUCA, use it to reshape Malaysia’s universities, says UTM VC
items.summary: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) vice-chancellor Prof Dr Mohd Shafry Mohd Rahim said the change needed to be supported by a legal framework that could nurture knowledge, intellectual courage and creativity in line with technological, economic and geopolitical changes. He said UTM welcomed the aspirations of the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) to implement the transformation in a comprehensive and responsible manner. “Therefore, higher education legislation must evolve in line with changing times, without neglecting institutional stability and public interest,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Future of Likas Wetlands, one of world’s only two city mangrove Ramsar sites, hangs in balance with mega project next door
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — The Likas Wetlands – only two of its kind in the world located within a city and enjoys global Ramsar status – may cease to exist within 15 years if nothing is done to prevent polluted water from a nearby mega project infiltrating the 24-hectare gazetted site and killing the vegetation. Sabah Wetland Conservation Society President, Datuk Zainie Abdul Aucasa who sounded the alarm bell was apparently referring to massive development coming up in the vicinity near Hakka Hall in Likas. Zaini said the Society would not waver or fail from its commitment to preserving the mangroves in the KK wetlands and defending its Ramsar status, the wetlands equivalent of World Heritage site.

items.title: DAP delegates have spoken, respect their decision, Kon Yeow tells Rafizi over unity govt stance
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow today told Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli to respect the party and its delegates’ decision to remain in the unity government. Chow said this was a basic principle following Rafizi’s comments on the resolution adopted at DAP’s congress yesterday. “We ask Rafizi to respect DAP and the decision of its delegates.

items.title: Penang’s undersea tunnel still on the map, draft plan keeps idea alive for 2040
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — The proposed undersea tunnel or third bridge linking Penang island to the mainland was included as an indicative proposal in the Draft Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (RSN Penang 2040), Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said the project remain in the draft plan as the agreement with the appointed company is still valid, although its eventual implementation would depend on development schedules. He said the draft RSN Penang 2040 should serve as a “compass” for the state’s development.

items.title: Ranau court fines duo RM3,500 each after Sabah police link their wrist marks to illegal militant Philippine group
items.summary: RANAU, Aug 17 — Two men were each fined RM3,500 by the Ranau Magistrate’s Court for being members of a Philippine organisation deemed illegal under the Societies Act 1966 – the latest in such cases in the district. Roy Martin, 35, a farmer, and Mohd Sharin Ibrahim, 40, a tyre mechanic, were charged under Section 43 of the Societies Act 1966 for being members of Kappa Rho Kappa (KRK), also referred to in the investigation as the Knights of the Right Keppers, a Philippines-based militant organisation. According to the case documents, a team from the D7 Criminal Investigation Department (JSJ) of the Sabah Police Contingent Headquarters, led by Insp Jesmera bin Bandong, conducted checks on the two men at the premises.

items.title: Century‑old Penang Hill railway gets track and roof repairs in scheduled January 2027 break
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 17 — Penang Hill’s iconic funicular will take a short break from January 4 to 10, 2027 for its scheduled bi annual maintenance, Penang Hill Corporation (PHC) announced today. Service is set to resume on January 11. During the closure, visitors can use the jeep service operated by the Penang Hill Jeep Service Association near the Penang Botanic Gardens Department Office, or take existing hiking routes to the summit.

items.title: No water for nearly two months, then a RM120,000 bill — Putatan condo dwellers ask why pay for water Sabah water utility was already treating
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 17 — Residents of Kingfisher Putatan Condominium (KFP) are refusing to pay the more than RM120,000 bill for water delivered by privately-operated tankers when they endured 55 days without supply between April and May. Some said they had no choice but to purchase bottled water for drinking, washing, cooking, cleaning and other daily needs. Despite being located just south of Kota Kinabalu, Putatan has faced repeated water shortages since 2018.

items.title: Sarawak forest fire in Daro enters eighth day, 4ha still burning
items.summary: DARO, Aug 17 — Firefighters are on their eighth day of working to extinguish a forest fire in Kampung Kut here, which has affected about 29ha of land. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said in a statement that firefighters are working to completely extinguish the remaining hotspots of the forest fire. Firefighters from the Daro fire station were deployed to three sectors during the operation.

items.title: Kuching man loses RM104,310 after falling for WhatsApp scam from friend’s hijacked account
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 17 — A 49-year-old man here lost RM104,310 to a phone scam last week. Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the victim was contacted via WhatsApp from a friend’s number, but it turned out the account had been hacked and hijacked. “Having trusted the message, the victim then made four transfers to three different accounts from Aug 13 to Aug 15, amounting to a total sum of RM104,310.

items.title: Johor businessman’s body bound in net, dumped in river; four accused face murder charge
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Aug 17 — Four men were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here with murdering a businessman, whose body was bound and covered in a net before being found in a river earlier this month. The accused — S. Yogesvaran, 40; Lim Yong Ming, 26; N. Achutan, 32; and How Han Wei, 33 — nodded to indicate they understood the charge after it was read before Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno in Bahasa Melayu. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution, while Yogesvaran, Yong Ming and Han Wei were represented by counsel S.J.

items.title: Pantai firefighters extinguish blaze on Jalan Kerinchi, BMW destroyed, Axia 30 per cent damaged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 17 — A BMW was destroyed and a Perodua Axia partially damaged after a blaze broke out at KL Gateway Mall, Jalan Kerinchi, last night. The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call via the NG999 line at 9.53pm before dispatching six firefighters from the Pantai station to the scene, New Straits Times reported. Operations commander Mokhtar Ramli said firefighters found two vehicles at the scene — the BMW was completely gutted, while the Perodua Axia sustained about 30 per cent damage.

items.title: Sarawak air quality improves as Serian and Samarahan drop from unhealthy to moderate
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 17 — Sarawak recorded moderate air quality at all monitoring stations except Bario, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading remained at good level as of 8am on Monday, according to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s Daily Haze Watch. Air quality in Serian and Samarahan improved from unhealthy levels — with API readings of 157 and 151 respectively at 4pm on Sunday — to moderate levels of 98 and 92 by 8am. However, three areas recorded slight increases in API readings.

items.title: Man, 35, dies after motorcycle strikes lorry left without fuel on Tumpat flyover
items.summary: TUMPAT, Aug 17 — A 35-year-old motorcyclist was killed when his Yamaha 135LC struck the rear of a parked lorry on the Wakaf Bharu flyover here yesterday evening. The accident happened at about 5pm as the victim was riding from Kota Bharu towards Pengkalan Kubor, Berita Harian (BH) reported. Tumpat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said the lorry had been left on the left shoulder of the flyover after running out of fuel.

items.title: Religious leaders launch Tabung Haji RCI outreach, clarify misuse risks and safeguard 9.7 million depositors’ savings
items.summary: Former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said the initiative would see Islamic scholars and religious figures explaining the RCI TH findings through mosques, surau, schools, government departments, colleges, universities and community education platforms. He said the initiative followed a special conference, Hifz al-Mal, which brought together more than 100 scholars and religious leaders from across the country yesterday to discuss the findings and the responsibility of safeguarding the savings of 9.7 million depositors. “What makes the conference particularly significant is that it brought together religious figures alongside professionals and scholars from various fields, including chartered accountants, economic commentators, legal practitioners, religious educators and pondok scholars.
